items.heading: Turmeric, lime and kumkum at the entrance
details: Turmeric is a natural antiseptic, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory agent, and lime is naturally alkaline - together applied at the threshold, they form a simple chemical barrier against insects and airborne bacteria.
Culturally, the combination is considered auspicious and associated with cleanliness, inviting positive energy into the home.

items.heading: Neem leaves at the entrance
details: Neem contains compounds with insect-repellent and insecticidal properties, helping keep pests away from the doorway.

items.heading: Mango-leaf toran
details: Fresh greenery hung at the entrance is traditional, and may carry minor plant-related ecological or insect-deterrent effects.

items.heading: Rice-flour Kolam / Muggu / Rangoli
details: Drawing the intricate geometric pattern each morning encourages concentration, fine-motor coordination, and spatial processing.
Using edible rice flour also feeds ants, birds, and small creatures right at the doorstep, keeping them occupied outside rather than indoors.

items.heading: Cow-dung coated traditional floors
details: Dried, properly prepared cow-dung mixtures can harden earthen floors and reduce dust.
Scientific analysis has shown cow dung to have disinfectant and antibacterial properties, useful in traditional mud-and-thatch homes.

items.heading: Raised traditional entrance / plinth
details: A raised entrance or plinth helps reduce the entry of rainwater, mud, and surface moisture into the home.

items.heading: Lighting oil lamps (Diya) and incense (Agarbatti)
details: The warm glow and gentle flicker of a flame uplift mood and create a calm, serene atmosphere for prayer.
Traditionally, the oils and ghee used as fuel are believed to purify the air and repel insects, and incense smoke masks household odors.

items.heading: Hanging a pumpkin, lemon, and chillies (Drishti Bommai)
details: In folk tradition, this wards off the "evil eye" or negative energy from jealousy and heavy foot traffic.
The sour, pungent smell of hanging lemons and chillies genuinely repels many pests, and once the produce spoils it is simply discarded.
